summary: GEMSDOE32 owner pages attach different numeric labels to the same anchor file: the index labels it 0.2708, while an audit record calls the same SHA-256 the 0.2600 reference anchor. The byte/mask identity is reproducible locally, but neither numeric label establishes an organizer score.
evidence: SHA-256 4dc4cc54b061cb4567a5500c8fa2bfe750a39340b02c8cdbb4308916f36cbcc3; sibling audit record says in_footprint_values_bit_identical_to_anchor=true and positive_px 44090; mask equality with a prior GEMSDOE25 artifact measured true here. Numeric labels are owner-published only.
status: OPEN AS A PROVENANCE/LABELING DISCREPANCY - do not treat 0.2600 or 0.2708 as an organizer-returned score. The file identity does not establish performance or a causal effect.

summary: The three geodetic layers satisfy no exact algebraic identity, so the invariant convention behind geod_2ndinv is not recoverable.
evidence: Tested on 5,164,312 in-footprint pixels: sqrt(dil^2+shear^2) max |error| 33.8 on a field with median 19.9 (best r = 0.9934); sqrt((dil^2+shear^2)/2), sqrt(dil^2+2 shear^2), |dil|+|shear| all worse. geod_2ndinv >= |shear| holds everywhere but geod_2ndinv >= |dil| holds only 82% of the time.
status: OPEN - Stage 1 is stated in quantile space, which is invariant to the unknown convention.

summary: Any feature derived from the catalogue is a perfect training leak in a blocked holdout.
evidence: With d_cat and cat_dens in the feature matrix, in-block AUC was exactly 0.500 while the physical features alone reach 0.63; removing them recovered in-block AUC to 0.667. Cause: every training positive is itself a catalogue pixel, so d_cat == 0 for all positives and > 0 for all negatives.
status: CLOSED - catalogue-derived columns excluded from the model, used only at emission time.

summary: The provenance of the hidden test faults is deliberately undisclosed, so no competitor can tell whether the labels are topographic, geophysical or field-mapped. Phase 2's test set is rebuilt from expert review of Phase 1 submissions.
evidence: chrisk-dd, 2026-09-23, community thread 11527 post 7: "We're not sharing details about the data sources, fault types, or coverage behind the test faults beyond what's in the problem description." And: "the largest prize pool (Phase 2) will use a test set that is updated by expert review of all Phase 1 submissions, so your fault predictions have an impact on final evaluation even if they are not the most performant in Phase 1."
status: RESOLVED - no answer will come. Consequence: (a) every validation instrument here is calibrated against the visible catalogue and may not match the hidden label style; (b) Phase 1 submissions are not free - they are inputs to Phase 2's test set, so geological defensibility of the emitted dots matters beyond this round's score.

summary: The local labels raster is byte-identical to the existing-known-fault raster, consistent with the official description of training labels as existing USGS/INGENIOUS faults; this is not evidence that the organizer training labels are missing.
evidence: Official problem page says training labels are known USGS/INGENIOUS faults and the initial hidden test set contains expert-identified faults absent from that database. Local data/labels.tif and data/existing_faults.tif have the same SHA-256 and element-wise values; the local catalogue mask matches them. Therefore local hide-and-recover holdouts measure known-fault recovery only, not performance on the hidden new-fault target.
status: CORRECTED 2026-10-07 - local metrics are proxy evidence; obtain organizer-authenticated challenge data if needed to validate exact provenance, but do not describe known-fault training labels as unavailable merely because they match existing_faults.tif.
